question: On kibble, does the evidence review's required-parts check work: does it ask for the parts a job's success line really requires, and does it find them in a result when, and only when, they are there?
unit: One result and one part the checker asks for. 'required' is whether the success line really asks for that part; 'present' is whether the result contains it (only judged when required).
selection: Kibble job IDs (generation 0, archive of 20 October 2026) whose success line yields at least one part, with a result posted after the job; the 20 with the lowest sha256('KIBBLE-EXP-001 development ' + ID); the first such result.
labelled_by: By hand from the success line and result text, before the checker's presence results were seen (see this file's commit). The parts the checker asks for were visible; whether it finds them was not.

cases.why: 'the 3 config keys/values': the result gives one.
'10 consecutive runs' is a test condition, not ten items to list.
'one read-only URL': none given.
No URL.
'rounded to two decimals' is not two items.
'at least three distinct vulnerability reports': the result refuses.
'exactly three ordinance titles': the result says it cannot.
'two decimals' again.
'the query + the index': no SQL, only the job restated.
Two numbered causes with kubectl commands.
'a table of 3 criteria': none, the job restated.
'Completed work … successfully.'
Job restated, no SQL.
'Completed work … successfully.'
'a sample query joining all three models': a worked example, not SQL; 'three models' are not three items to list.
'defines result_hash' names a term, not a hash value; 'N>=2 jobs' is not two items.
'2 concrete bugs': numbered 1. and 2.
Same job wording as kb3bc4ce45d.
'at least 4 distinct test cases': the result names one command and no test cases.
'Completed work … successfully.'
